standard_prerequisites.name: n-types and contractibility
standard_prerequisites.statement: X is a (-2)-type if it is contractible and an (n+1)-type if all its path spaces are n-types.
standard_prerequisites.use: The base case at source lines 121-128 is stated for contractible types and the induction step at lines 130-132 is exactly the path-space definition.

standard_prerequisites.name: Contractibility as a pair of centre and contraction
standard_prerequisites.statement: A contractible type comes with a centre a_0 and, for every x, a path contr_x : a_0 = x.
standard_prerequisites.use: The centre and the contraction are what build the candidate centre contr_x `ct` opp(contr_y) at source line 124.

standard_prerequisites.name: Path induction
standard_prerequisites.statement: To prove a family of statements about p : x = y for all p it suffices to prove it at refl x.
standard_prerequisites.use: It reduces the contraction obligation at source lines 126-128 to refl x = contr_x `ct` opp(contr_x).

core_obligations: Base case n = -2: for a contractible type A with centre a_0 and contraction contr, show that x = y is contractible for all x, y : A, choosing contr_x `ct` opp(contr_y) as the centre (source lines 121-125).

Show that this centre is indeed a centre, i.e. that p = contr_x `ct` opp(contr_y) for any p : x = y; by path induction it suffices to verify refl x = contr_x `ct` opp(contr_x), which is trivial (source lines 126-128).
Induction step: given that X is an (n+1)-type, apply the inductive hypothesis to the path space x = y, which is an n-type, to conclude that it is also an (n+1)-type (source lines 130-132).

proof_roadmap.step: Set up the induction on n.
Base case: contractible types have contractible path spaces, with an explicit centre and contraction.
Induction step by applying the hypothesis to the path space.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 7.1.7 at source lines 113-116: if X is an n-type and n >= -2 then X is also an (n+1)-type. The proof (source lines 118-133) is short but its base case is a nontrivial computation: one must show that the path space of a contractible type is contractible, which means producing the centre contr_x `ct` opp(contr_y) for arbitrary endpoints x, y (source line 124) and then proving at lines 126-128 that any p : x = y equals it, a step that only closes after path induction, where it becomes the triviality refl x = contr_x `ct` opp(contr_x). The induction step at lines 130-132 is then a single application of the hypothesis, so the whole weight of the theorem is in the boundary case n = -2 that the retained context flags.
